g.text: Bloom Filter: 16 bits, k=2 hash functions
Two short codes inserted, then two lookups against the same bit array
Both bits are 1 -> "possibly present" -- correct, it really was inserted.
Query("codeZZ01") -- never inserted, checks bits 5 and 2
Both bits are already 1 (set by A and B) -> FALSE POSITIVE. This item was never inserted.
More bits per item = lower false-positive rate. ~10 bits/item tunes to well under 1% FP rate --
a memory win that's the same whether each item is 8 bytes or 8 kilobytes, since only bits are stored.
No deletion: clearing a bit for one item can un-set it for another that hashed to the same position.
